question: According to media reports, EUR 4 billion worth of COVID-19 vaccines, ordered by the President of the Commission Ursula von der Leyen from Albert Bourla at Pfizer, had to be disposed of in 2023 due to lack of demand. 1.
At what cost and at who's expense was this done, and to what extent can it be expected that the remaining superfluous COVID-19 vaccines will be disposed of over the course of 2024?

In what ways can Ursula von der Leyen be held civilly liable for her poor use of billions of euros on purchases made in disregard of public tendering law, especially considering that there is a threshold of EUR 140 000 in place for Union-wide public tenders?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.6.2024) As the Commission pointed out in its reply to written question E-003751/2023, Member States are the legal owners of the COVID-19 vaccines procured through (Advance) Purchase Agreements concluded by the Commission on behalf of the Member States with vaccine manufacturers. Member States are thus responsible for overseeing the management of their national stockpiles.

Therefore, the Commission is not in a position to provide figures on the volume of stockpiles and any associated costs linked to their management and disposal. The maintenance of strategic stockpiles in Member States is a usual practice to ensure access to sufficient vaccine doses to protect citizens in light of the uncertainty over the epidemiological evolution of COVID-19.

The Commission stresses that all the contracts with vaccine developers were concluded in accordance with the applicable procurement rules. They were negotiated jointly by the Commission and the Member States in accordance with the agreement with Member States on procuring COVID-19 vaccines on behalf of the Member States and related procedures1.

Before each contract was concluded, it was submitted to the Member States to ensure that they agreed with all contractual terms and conditions that were negotiated with the companies. They were, moreover, entitled to opt out from the contracts.
